name: close-location-subsignal
rationale: The 2026-09-21 run produced this pipeline's strongest negative result and its clearest instruction for what to do next. Inverting 100% of the aggregated TA composite (contrarian-composite-inversion) moved the 500,000 JPY return by only 0.41pp (-10.8368 -> -10.4301) on a run whose fee_drag_pct was 5.85, with the instrumentation confirming the flip was bit-exact over all 15,865 evaluated bars. A signal with a real negative edge would have swung symmetrically; near-invariance under a total sign flip is the signature of a composite carrying approximately ZERO directional information. That report's lead #3 draws the consequence explicitly: the entire 'adjust the signal's gain, sign or weighting' family is a dead end, and the productive direction is a GENUINELY DIFFERENT signal -- a new indicator or data source, not a reweighting of the existing five sub-signals. This hypothesis is the cheapest such test available, and it is only testable at all since 2026-09-09. All five current sub-signals (RSI, SMA cross, EMA cross, MACD histogram, Bollinger %B) are functions of the CLOSE series alone. The high and the low of each bar are fetched, stored and aggregated but never reach compute_btc_target. Under the CoinGecko series this pipeline used until 2026-09-09 that was not a loss, because every row had open == high == low == close (2161/2161 rows measured, per docs/self-improvement-loop.md), so intra-bar range carried literally no information. On the bitFlyer execution tape the bars now have true intra-bar range, so the close's position inside its own bar -- (close - low) / (high - low), the 'close fraction' or close location value -- is a real, orthogonal observable that this strategy has never used. It is a microstructure quantity, not a smoothed price transform: it measures where within the minute's realised range the market settled, i.e. which side won the bar, and it is by construction uncorrelated with the LEVEL that all five existing sub-signals key off. This also matters because of what it is NOT: it is not another gain/weighting knob, so it is not covered by the dead-end verdict above, and its neutral value (0.5 on a bar that closes mid-range) is exactly the composite's neutral point, so adding it cannot introduce a directional bias by construction. The honest prior is weak -- see paper_reference's cons, and note the paper's own directional-accuracy gain is 0.04pp -- but the point of this run is to establish whether ANY orthogonal information source moves this strategy at all, and a 14-day holdout answering 'no' to a cheap additive sub-signal is itself worth recording against lead #3.
code_change_summary: Add the bar's intra-bar high and low to IndicatorPoint and use them as ONE new sub-signal inside TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. Three edits, no more. (1) In src/signal/mod.rs, add two fields to IndicatorPoint -- `pub high: Option<f64>` and `pub low: Option<f64>` -- immediately after the existing `close` field, each with an English doc comment saying they carry the bar's realised intra-bar range and are consumed by compute_btc_target's close-location sub-signal. Populate them in compute_indicators() from the same Candle the existing `close` field is taken from, using the identical Decimal -> f64 conversion path already used there (ToPrimitive::to_f64), so the new fields are None in exactly the cases `close` is None. Do not change how any indicator is constructed, updated or reset, and do not change the order of the map. If any other construction site of IndicatorPoint exists (tests, src/api/routes/indicators.rs, src/signal/engine.rs, the backtest simulator), update it to the new struct shape in the least invasive way possible -- prefer populating the real values where a Candle is in hand and None where one is not; if IndicatorPoint derives Default, prefer ..Default::default() in test constructors. (2) In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), after the Bollinger %B sub-signal push and BEFORE the `if sub_signals.is_empty()` warmup guard, push exactly one additional sub-signal computed by a new named private helper with a doc comment giving the formula and its range -- e.g. `fn close_location(close: f64, high: f64, low: f64) -> f64 { let range = high - low; if range > 0.0 { ((close - low) / range).clamp(0.0, 1.0) } else { 0.5 } }` -- guarded by `if let (Some(close), Some(high), Some(low)) = (raw.close, raw.high, raw.low)` and pushed with TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, because a close settling in the upper part of its own bar's range is a momentum/buying-pressure reading, not a mean-reverting one. A zero or negative range (a bar where every print was at one price, which does occur on thin minutes) MUST map to exactly 0.5, matching how the existing Bollinger arm handles flat bands. (3) Nothing else. Do NOT change damped_cross, CROSS_SATURATION, REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT's value, any existing sub-signal's formula or the family weight it is pushed with, the weighted-mean aggregation or its divisor, the warmup guard, the sentiment path, the ta_weight/sentiment_weight combination, or the final clamp. Note in a NOTE comment that this raises the realised weight_sum for a fully-warm point from 2.75 to 3.00 and that this is the intended, and only, dilution of the existing sub-signals. Add unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs: (a) a point whose close sits at its bar's high, asserting the new sub-signal contributes its maximum and that the composite is strictly greater than the same point with close at the bar's low; (b) a point with high == low == close asserting the sub-signal contributes exactly 0.5 and that the composite equals what the pre-change code would have produced for the same point, i.e. degenerate bars are a no-op; (c) a point with high and low as None asserting the sub-signal is skipped entirely and the composite is byte-identical to the old formula's value for that point (this is the backward-compatibility pin); (d) an all-None IndicatorPoint asserting the warmup guard still returns None. Also add a unit test in src/signal/mod.rs asserting compute_indicators() populates high and low from the candle. Update any existing compute_btc_target_* test whose expected value legitimately changes because weight_sum moved from 2.75 to 3.00, and do not weaken or delete a test to make it pass. Additionally instrument and REPORT (stderr logging or a scratch harness ONLY -- do NOT add a field to BacktestReport) the realised mean and standard deviation of the close-location sub-signal over the evaluated window, and the fraction of evaluated bars whose range was zero, so the coordinator can tell an inert sub-signal apart from an ineffective one.
constraints: This hypothesis DOES modify TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's body. That is permitted under experiments/hypotheses/README.md's '`compute_btc_target` may be modified' section, but ONLY on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch, and it MUST be reported explicitly so the coordinator flags it in any PR description.
MUST NOT change compute_btc_target's SIGNATURE. Only its body may change.

MUST NOT change any EXISTING sub-signal's formula, damped_cross, CROSS_SATURATION, REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT's value, the family weight each existing sub-signal is pushed with, the weighted-mean aggregation or its divisor, the empty-sub_signals warmup guard returning None, the sentiment normalization, the ta_weight/sentiment_weight combination, or the final clamp. The ONLY behavioural change is one ADDITIONAL sub-signal.
MUST NOT touch apply_zone, sticky_target, block_start, allocation_delta_to_order, the lot-size check, the orders_below_min counting arm, the RiskManager call sequence, or the fee logic.

MUST NOT introduce a tunable constant. The close-location mapping is exact ((close - low) / (high - low), clamped, with a 0.5 fallback on a degenerate range) and the sub-signal reuses the EXISTING TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT rather than a new weight of its own. If a different weight looks better, that is a separate hypothesis to propose, not a value to tune mid-run.
MUST NOT fit anything on the holdout window, or on any window at all.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including every existing compute_btc_target_* unit test. Update an expected value only where the added sub-signal legitimately changes it, and do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass.

MUST NOT change src/signal/engine.rs's broadcast cadence or anything about live scheduling. Adding two fields to IndicatorPoint and populating them is permitted; changing when or how often an IndicatorPoint is produced is not.

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body and adds a sub-signal to the allocation formula the live engine acts on.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the order-submission mechanics themselves.

paper_reference.title: Enhancing OHLC Data with Timing Features: A Machine Learning Evaluation
paper_reference.key_claim: Intra-bar structure beyond the close carries incremental predictive information in 1-minute OHLC bars: the paper's feature set includes 'Close Fraction', the close price's position on a 0-1 scale between the bar's low and high, and the full feature set improves out-of-sample directional accuracy from 72.106% to 72.147% and test NLL from 0.4088 to 0.4075 against a no-timing baseline.
paper_reference.pros: Same bar resolution shirube trades at (1-minute), and the feature is exactly the quantity shirube stores but never uses -- the close's location inside its own bar's realised high-low range. It requires no new data source, only that the bars have genuine intra-bar range, which has been true of shirube's series since the bitFlyer execution tape replaced CoinGecko on 2026-09-09. It is orthogonal by construction to all five current sub-signals, which are functions of the close series alone, and it is therefore the cheapest available test of the 2026-09-21 report's lead #3 (that a genuinely different signal, not another reweighting, is the only productive direction left).
paper_reference.cons: Russell 3000 US equities in calendar year 2021, not bitFlyer BTC/JPY spot in 2026 -- a different instrument, a different microstructure, and a market with fixed session hours whose bar boundaries mean something they do not in 24/7 crypto. Transaction costs were NOT modeled at all, which is disqualifying on its own for a strategy whose fee_drag_pct (5.97 at 500,000 JPY on 2026-09-21) exceeds its return. The paper predicts VWAP returns, not an allocation target, so the mapping onto shirube's use is an analogy rather than a transfer. It never isolates the close-location feature's own contribution -- the reported gain belongs to the whole timing feature set -- and that gain is 0.04 percentage points of directional accuracy, well inside the range that would vanish under any realistic cost model. Treated strictly as a reason to spend one slot testing an orthogonal observable, not as evidence that it will work.
